in_hebrew.name: פסקלה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The Hebrew name Pascale is derived from the Hebrew word 'Pesach', which means 'Passover'. This name was traditionally given to girls born during the Jewish Passover festival, as a reminder of the Exodus from Egypt and the liberation of the Israelites.

in_greek.name: Πασκαλη
in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek name Pascale is derived from the Greek word 'Paskha', which means 'Easter'. This name was given to girls in honor of the Christian celebration of the Resurrection of Jesus Christ.

in_latin.name: Pascalis
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name Pascalis is derived from the Latin word 'Paschale', which means 'Of Passover'. This name was used to honor the Christian celebration of the Resurrection of Jesus Christ, which is traditionally celebrated during the season of Passover.

biblical_reference.note: The name Pascale is mentioned in the Bible in connection with the Jewish Passover festival. The Israelites were instructed to mark their doors with the blood of a lamb to protect their homes from the Angel of Death. This practice became a symbol of God's protection and provision, and the name Pascale has since been given to girls born during the Passover season.
